timecoded_text_to_speech.text: We're here at ITU Telecom World 2015 in Budapest, Hungary and I'm very pleased to be joined
by Vanessa and Boutesi who won the second annual Miss Geek Prize at a contest sponsored
by the Rwandan government to spur girls involvement in ICTs. Vanessa, welcome to the studio.
Thank you.
Now I'd like to talk to you about this Miss Geek Prize. I mean it's a funny name but
it sounds like a very worthy prize. Please tell us a little bit about Miss Geek 2015 and
essentially how it felt to win the award and what it means.
Well Miss Geek was started by girls in ICT which is an organisation started by girls in
ICT in Rwanda and it's there to encourage girls to follow careers in sciences and technology.
This year was actually quite challenging because I was going against very intelligent girls
and it was overall a great experience not only meeting people who trained us to do our
public speaking correctly but as well as having a platform for us to show our ideas because
a lot of countries you go to there's like very little women involvement in ICT so I wanted to
show that girls can do have a voice in that area. When I won the award it was a bit nerve wrecking
presenting to a room for people who is never easy and being the youngest contestant that they've
had is even more pressure because also your girls were either in college or their last year of
high school. Because you're only 15 is that right? Yes. Recently 16 actually. Okay, you're
recent birthday. So that's great so you're up against much older girls than you and you're still
one with that's brilliant. So tell us a little bit about the idea that won the prize. I believe
it's called Rwanda Online Open School. What does this solution do and what are the benefits of people?
So Rwanda Online Open School was inspired by children in Rwanda because some schools in
no income schools they don't have enough resources and this hinders people the children's education.
So what Rwanda Online Open School focused on is having a platform where they have all their textbooks
the school curriculum school calendar everything on a server so that no one has to either borrow
textbook or wait for someone to finish using the textbook but you have your own access to this.
Children will be able to interact across the country because obviously teachers are not always
going to be there so you have to use the people around you your peers to solve solutions to come
up with answers to your problems. So I want to also impact students to have that proactive
manner inside of them whereby they don't have to wait for someone to do something for them
but also what they can do for themselves. One of the biggest benefits in using Rwanda Online
Open School is that children will be able to be proactive in their education. They don't have to
wait for the teacher to do something for them but they can also do for the teacher something for
the school and give back but as well as promote parental involvement in the children's academic
lives because sometimes parents aren't able to follow what their children are doing in school so
the children can use that as an excuse to lie behind in school or they can just leave it alone
and just give up on school itself. So we want to promote that parental involvement in the
children's life because when you have your parents involved in your academic life to encourage you
or to push you because I know my mother pushes me a lot to do better. It will help you it does even
though it's sometimes tough love it does help you to get farther so help teachers communicate
with parents tell you it's for your child's doing well if your child's not doing well or if there
are any community events that they can get involved in so that they can do as much as a community.
And you mentioned your mother I'm wondering if there were any role models if there are any
particular people that influenced you and that it encouraged you or spurs you on to have an
interesting ICTs. Yes my sister her name is Lucy she is a big a big geek and she's actually proud
of it so she's been one of my biggest motivations because she has always been pushed by her own
inspiration to be one of the women in Randa who's spurs on women in ICT but as always my mother
because she's a very very strong woman I find and she's always inspired me to do better and to do
to go above what I can do and always know that where I've come from and how I can also help
my people get to where I am or even farther. Is Rwanda nurturing environment for young people in
ICTs? Yes definitely because as technology is growing a lot in Randa and you find a lot of people
social media is big buzz in Randa and there's a lot of there's a lot of young people and I feel like
they treat us at a very high level of respect because they see that we are the future of tomorrow
whereby they take in our ideas they think about it they help you they nurture your ideas they guide
you so I feel like they're doing a very wonderful job overall of making sure that we have the best
that we can get so that we can also give back to our country what it's given to us. Now I don't
know about your geographical travels but I presume this is your first time in Budapest is that right?
In Hungary and and your first time at ITU Telecom World I would imagine too. I just wanted to find out
what have been your impressions of this event. This event has been a wonderful event and I feel
like I'm very blessed to be here because I've met a lot of people it's not so often that you can
enter a space where there's a bunch of countries altogether coming from different places in the
world Azerbaijan India all in one place it's not often that you get to have such interaction
especially when you come from East Africa and you meet people who are from India it's obvious
that you can't meet them as frequently so it has been a good networking platform but as well as
it's a good experience looking what different people do looking at how we can help each other
coming from different places of the world just because you're far away doesn't mean I can't help
you or you can't help me. Well Vanessa that's great thank you so much for joining us in this
idea today it's been really good and I really wish you all the best with your future career it's
it sounds like you've got a very promising one so thank you well done thank you
